REDINGTON

Apple may limit price hikes for the iPhone 18 Pro despite component costs expected to jump 38%, according to TrendForce.

Soaring memory prices are the main driver, with memory projected to exceed 40% of component costs by early 2027, up from just 10% a year earlier.

To protect demand, Apple could accept lower profit margins—or raise prices on older iPhones to offset the added costs

Ola Electric | Q1 Business Update

Business Performance
- Deliveries 39,192 units (+94% QoQ).
- Auto Revenue ₹455 Cr (+72% QoQ).
- Registrations +97% QoQ.
- E2W industry growth 17%.
- Market Share 8.4% (vs 5.1%).
- Gross Margin 30.5%.

Cost Optimisation
- Operating Expenses ₹333 Cr (-22% QoQ).
- Steady-state cost target ~₹300 Cr/month.
- FY26 operational reset improved execution.
- Higher operating leverage expected.

Balance Sheet
- Raised ₹780 Cr through QIP.
- QIP oversubscribed by 56%.
- Balance sheet strengthened.
- Received one-time PLI benefit.

Operational Highlights
- Orders 44,071 units.
- Deliveries reached 39,192 units.
- West region sales +61% QoQ.
- North region sales +54% QoQ.
- South region sales +54% QoQ.
- East region sales +34% QoQ.

Technology & Growth Drivers
- AI integrated across operations.
- AI improved appointment conversions 47%.
- AI increased sales conversions 17%.
- Cell Gigafactory to reach 6 GWh by September.
- 4680 LFP cell received BIS certification.
- Vehicle rollout planned for scooters below 4 kWh.
- Mahashakti energy storage platform launches 15 August.
- Targets renewable, industrial & data centre markets.
- Axis Energy partnership for 20 GWh battery storage by 2032.
- MoUs signed for defence, UAVs and near-space applications.

Management Commentary
- Supportive EV policy environment.
- India's E2W penetration crossed 10%.
- Focus on market share gains.
- Improving productivity through AI.
- Cost optimisation continues.
- Scale expected to drive profitability.
- Expanding beyond EV applications.

Key Positives
- Strong delivery growth.
- Market share improved.
- Healthy gross margins.
- Operating costs reduced.
- Successful QIP fundraising.
- AI-led productivity gains.
- Battery manufacturing progressing.
- New energy storage opportunities.
- Defence and industrial diversification.

Key Concerns
- Profitability yet to stabilize.
- Execution of Gigafactory ramp-up.
- Dependence on EV demand growth.
- Competitive industry landscape.

Key Monitorables
- Delivery momentum.
- Market share gains.
- Cost reduction progress.
- Operating leverage.
- Cell Gigafactory commissioning.
- Battery storage order pipeline.
- Margin sustainability.

Impact
- Positive.
- Strong operational recovery.
- Cost structure improving.
- Technology investments gaining traction.
- Long-term growth opportunities expanding.

Key Takeaway
- Ola Electric reported a strong operational recovery in Q1 with sharp improvements in deliveries, market share and revenue while continuing to reduce costs. AI-led productivity, battery manufacturing, energy storage expansion and diversification into defence and industrial applications provide multiple long-term growth drivers, although sustained profitability remains the key monitorable.

📈 The kiosk-led model supports an asset-light, scalable expansion strategy, enabling efficient growth, better retail productivity, and long-term market penetration across urban centres. 

💡 Overall, this strategic move aligns with Recode’s vision of building a strong omnichannel network, driving sustainable growth, customer loyalty, and enhanced market reach across India.

text: Arc (Equity) - Extended pause; data to guide rate re-calibration

**CITI on Hindalco
Neutral, TP Rs 1175**

Novelis reported 1Q adj E

BITDA at $516m vs. $416m – lower scrap prices and cost efficiencies helped.

Adj EBITDA/t: $563 vs. $544 in 4Q, $432 last year.

EBITDA includes $47m insurance recovery relating to business interruption (excluding this, EBITDA would be $469m, Citi est $460m).
Oswego impact: ~33k on volumes, EBITDA ~$29m.

Normalized EBITDA/t $525: excluding Oswego fires/insurance recovery. Volumes fell ~5% yoy to 916kt.

**Key highlights:**
(1) EBITDA/t upsides: As Oswego normalizes, tariff impact should taper down in a few quarters. Further, mgmt is confident about Bay Minette achieving EBITDA/t of $1,000.
(2) Insurance: Cash flow impact from the disruption to be $1.8bn vs. $1.7bn earlier ($1.4bn to date), insurance recoveries of ~$1.2bn, expect meaningful insurance recoveries going forward (1Q $300m, FY26 $90m).
(3) Cashflows/leverage:Net debt: $7.9bn vs. $6.7bn in Mar26; net D/EBITDA 4.5x vs. 4.1x. Mgmt expects working capital to normalize, net D/EBITDA at <4x by end FY28.

**CLSA on Hindalco
O-P, TP Rs 1240**

Novelis’ core profitability of US$525/t was in line, while adj Ebitda/t of US$563 was above.

Profitability improvement was driven by better scrap spreads and cost efficiencies, partly offset by higher tariffs.

In near term, resumption of Oswego since June (with a full ramp-up by 3QFY27) & a lower tariff impact, partly offset by normalising scrap spreads, should support profitability, according to Novelis.

It maintained Bay Minette profitability guidance of US$1,000/t-plus and blended Ebitda/t of US$600/t over the medium term.

After an increase in 1Q, Novelis expects exit-FY27 net debt to be lower, with leverage below 4x (1Q: 4.5x).

Jefferies on Hindalco
Hold, TP Rs 1075
Novelis' underlying business performance continues to be clouded by fire incident, buy impact is receding.
Excluding benefit of business interruption insurance proceeds, adjusted EBITDA grew 13% YoY, broadly in line with JEFe.
EBITDA/t contracted 6% QoQ to $512.
Novelis restarted its fire-affected facility in June and has started receiving insurance recoveries.
However, net debt continued to rise, up 17% QoQ to $7.9bn.

CITI om Navin Fluorine
Sell, TP Raised to Rs 7200
1Q EBITDA was up ~11% qoq, largely driven by higher HPP revenues (volumes+pricing).
EBITDA margin at 34.2% was flat qoq (vs. 28.5% in 1QFY26); mgmt continues to guide for sustainable EBITDA margin of 31–34%.
NFIL has initiated phase II of cGMP4 capex of Rs1.25bn to support demand for the existing molecule of a European CDMO major.
NFIL has also announced capex of Rs900m on adoption capacities to incubate products across semiconductor, electronics, and defense applications, providing medium-term growth visibility.
That said, NFIL is up 50% over past year, partly factoring in recent earnings strength
With downside risk to R32 pricing over next year (India industry capacity increasing from ~44ktpa to ~133ktpa; $1/kg change in R32 prices impacts NFIL’s FY28 EBITDA by 14%), think risk-reward is unfavorable.

Jefferies on Navin
Buy, TP Rs 9045
EBITDA/PAT 16%/25% ahead of JEFe, driven by HPP.
Strong pipeline in CDMO and cooling products, & participation in new molecules in spec chem anchor medium-term growth.
New capex in advanced materials will create another growth engine in medium-term
Upgrade FY27/28E PAT 8%/4% & project 23% EPS CAGR over FY26-29E.
Valuation is below LT average.

UBS on Navin Fluorine
Buy, TP Raised to Rs 9000
Strong start to FY27; growth momentum remains intact
Broad-based growth across business
CDMO continues to lead growth; Specialty and HPP remain strong

**Nomura on Cummins
Neutral, TP Rs 6000**

Sharper-than-expected gross margin dip leads to EBITDA miss

Revenue up 18%/14% y-y/q-q, beats estimates by 7%

EBITDA misses estimates by 4% led by sharper-than-expected gross margin contraction

To appoint new MD following Shveta Arya’s resignation

**Management’s outlook
Going forward, management expects –
1) steady business momentum across key markets;
2) inflationary pressures and supply-chain constraints influencing industry environment.**

**CITI on Cummins
Buy. TP Rs 6700**

1QFY27 below estimates.

Domestic demand strength (+22%YoY) led to revenue at Rs33.7bn growing 18%YoY, 5% ahead of Citie

However, margins were below expectations.

EBITDA margin fell 338bpsYoY to 16.7% (v/s 20.4% Citi/VAe) primarily as gross margins fell - impact of commodity headwinds/lag in pass-through was greater than expectations.

PAT at Rs5.4bn was flat YoY & 13% below estimates

Await clarity on any one-off expenditures in earnings call

Cummins India has notified that MD Shveta Arya has tendered her resignation to pursue external opportunities, effective 31 August.

**UBS on PB Fin
Sell, TP Rs 1660**

Revenue and profit beat driven by strong insurance growth
Renewal growth emerging as a key earnings driver
Growth strategy unchanged; regulatory discussions continue

**Nomura on PB Fin
Neutral, TP Rs 1590**

1QFY27 net profit beat of 21% vs est
Policybazaar & other insurance platforms: healthy improvement in take rates & contribution margins
Paisabazaar: core disbursals pick up momentum, new product launches lined up for Aug-26
Regulation still haunts us

**Bernstein on PB Fin
O-P, TP Rs 2310**

Execution continues to be strong.
Revenues grew +40% YoY, profits grew +92% YoY - both better than expected
While print was good, regulatory concerns persist
Insurance momentum continued (+41% YoY premia), driven by new health & term sales (+53% YoY).
They talked about a softer H2 growth (GST base effect), with renewals growing faster than fresh sales.
EBITDA and profit margin expansion continued
